project.name: Me.OpenClaw
project.description: Personal assistant that watches for vet expenses and does the insurance-claim legwork (bank charge -> Gmail invoice match -> Petcover PDF claim draft -> reply tracking), plus Gmail-based task/reminder capture onto a local dashboard.

nodes.name: agent.py
nodes.summary: Conversational Telegram agent: exposes read tools (query claims, pending actions, claim detail) and propose_* act tools over the claims domain to llm.chat's bounded tool loop; act tools never mutate directly, only queue a proposal the Telegram layer renders as a Confirm button.
nodes.languageNotes: Builds an LLM tool-calling schema (TOOLS) with closures capturing a per-turn proposals list, keeping mutation gated behind an explicit user confirmation tap.

nodes.name: claim_card.py
nodes.summary: Renders the /history claim card and the actions-summary card as PNG images using Pillow, since Telegram's plain-text rendering can't produce aligned tables or colour-coded status chips.
nodes.languageNotes: Draws at 2x supersample resolution then downsamples on save for anti-aliased text and chip corners.

nodes.name: claim_forms.py
nodes.summary: Fills the Petcover claim PDF form, extracts a claim's per-visit invoice pages from an email's PDF bundle, and creates (never sends) the Gmail draft — the core matched-to-drafted claim advancement plus the pet-split logic.

nodes.name: system_prompt
nodes.summary: Builds the agent's system prompt, injecting the real list of known pets and today's date so the model never has to guess either.

nodes.name: _find_claims
nodes.summary: Filters vet_claims joined with pet/transaction data by id, pet, reference, status, merchant or date range — the shared query behind every read tool.

nodes.name: _events_summary
nodes.summary: Renders a claim's recorded Petcover status events as short text lines for the chat agent's claim_history tool.

nodes.name: _build_impls
nodes.summary: Builds the closures backing every LLM tool call (query_claims, pending_actions, propose_* mutations, rematch_claims, poll_petcover_now, etc.), capturing a per-turn proposals list so act tools only ever queue a mutation rather than apply it.

nodes.name: handle_message
nodes.summary: Runs one chat turn: builds prompt+history+tool schema, calls llm.chat, and returns (reply_text, proposed_action) for the Telegram layer to render as a Confirm button.

nodes.name: _group_by_month
nodes.summary: Groups claim history rows into (month label, month total, rows) tuples, preserving newest-first order for the card layout.

nodes.name: totals
nodes.summary: Computes header totals for the claim history card: money actually reimbursed (settled only) vs. an excess/cap estimate for outstanding claims.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Draws one page of the claim history PNG card: header totals, month groupings, status-coloured chips and per-row detail.

nodes.name: _summarise
nodes.summary: Aggregates pending actions into (kind, title, count, total) tuples in first-seen order for the actions-summary card.

nodes.name: render_actions_summary
nodes.summary: Draws the actions-needed PNG overview, splitting actionable items from blocked ones into separate sections.

nodes.name: fill_petcover_form
nodes.summary: Fills the real Petcover fillable PDF form via pypdf, validating every expected field exists before writing and disabling auto-regenerate so pre-drawn radio/checkbox appearance streams render correctly.

nodes.name: _build_mime_message
nodes.summary: Builds a base64-encoded MIME message with attachments for the Gmail drafts API.

nodes.name: discard_claim_draft
nodes.summary: Deletes a Gmail draft this app created, by its message id, needed when a split makes an existing draft's amount wrong.

nodes.name: _shared_fields
nodes.summary: Builds the claim-form fields that are identical across every claim for a pet (owner, pet, bank details, declaration).

nodes.name: _group_by_condition
nodes.summary: Sums invoice item amounts per assigned condition for a multi-condition claim split.

nodes.name: apply_item_conditions
nodes.summary: Stores per-item condition assignments from the Telegram split flow, grouping items into form rows and advancing the claim.

nodes.name: find_invoice_segment
nodes.summary: Locates a claim's own per-visit invoice inside a multi-invoice PDF bundle by segmenting at invoice headers and matching total + patient name.

nodes.name: email_pdf_attachments
nodes.summary: Fetches every PDF attachment of an email as (filename, bytes).

nodes.name: _email_pdf_documents
nodes.summary: Every PDF attachment of an email as (PdfReader, per-page texts), skipping unreadable/corrupt attachments.

nodes.name: invoice_segment_pdf
nodes.summary: Extracts a claim-relevant invoice's pages from an email's PDF bundle as a standalone small PDF for review/merge Telegram alerts.

nodes.name: _write_invoice_file
nodes.summary: Writes a claim's sliced invoice pages to disk and records the path, clearing the awaiting-invoice flag.

nodes.name: ensure_invoice_file
nodes.summary: Extracts a claim's per-visit invoice pages from its matched email's PDF bundle (or a vision-OCR page) into their own file, flagging the claim when no adequate invoice can be found.

nodes.name: process_claim_batch
nodes.summary: Bundles up to 4 matched claims for one pet into a single filled claim form and Gmail draft, mirroring real multi-line Petcover submissions.

nodes.name: set_condition_text
nodes.summary: Shared update path for setting a claim's condition text, used by both the dashboard route and the Telegram /mark command.

nodes.name: assign_pet
nodes.summary: Shared update path for assigning a pet to a claim, used by both the dashboard route and the Telegram /pet command.

nodes.name: check_split
nodes.summary: Validates every guard on a pet-split (status, ceiling, duplicate pets, unstated-share limit) with no writes, so an impossible split is refused before Justin taps Confirm.

nodes.name: split_between_pets
nodes.summary: Apportions one invoice's claimable amount between pets: the original claim keeps the first share, and one new claim per remaining pet carries its own, discarding any superseded draft.

nodes.name: mark_reviewed
nodes.summary: Records that Justin has reviewed a drafted claim on Telegram — never touches status or the draft itself.

nodes.name: process_and_report
nodes.summary: Telegram /process: runs the matched-to-drafted advance for one claim on demand and reports the resulting state.

nodes.name: process_claim
nodes.summary: Advances a claim from matched to drafted once pet/process/condition/invoice are all present, filling the Petcover form and creating the Gmail draft; otherwise flags what's missing without guessing.

nodes.name: _vet_name
nodes.summary: Title-cases an all-caps NetBank vet descriptor while leaving already-mixed-case names untouched, clipped for card display.

nodes.name: claim_status.py
nodes.summary: The claim lifecycle state machine and single writer of vet_claims.status: classifies Petcover reply emails, applies/validates state transitions against an append-only event log, computes the excess/cap reimbursement ledger, and derives every dashboard/Telegram action list from that log.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements an explicit transition table (TRANSITIONS) plus an event-log fold (_fold/project_state) so a claim's authoritative state can be replayed from history rather than trusted from a mutable column.

nodes.name: db.py
nodes.summary: SQLite schema definition and connection management: defines every table (claims, events, split proposals, telegram messages), applies additive column migrations, and yields WAL-mode connections with a busy timeout.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses WAL journal mode specifically so a host-side read and a container-side write on the same bind-mounted file don't lock each other out.

nodes.name: invoice_matching.py
nodes.summary: Searches Gmail for the invoice matching a bank-charged vet transaction, extracts invoice data via LLM (with a vision-OCR fallback for scanned PDFs), and resolves one-charge-many-invoices and one-invoice-many-charges apportionment cases.
nodes.languageNotes: The bank charge is treated as a ceiling (not an equality target) on the claimable invoice total, per ADR-0007, to absorb card surcharges and multi-invoice charges.

nodes.name: extract_reference
nodes.summary: Extracts Petcover's claim reference, trying the stable shape pattern first (after stripping the policy number) and a context-phrase fallback second.

nodes.name: extract_sr
nodes.summary: Extracts Petcover's per-document serial number within a Condition Thread from either of two confirmed live text formats.

nodes.name: extract_settlement_amounts
nodes.summary: Extracts the older PDF-attachment settlement style's claimed/paid dollar amounts by regex.

nodes.name: extract_approval_amounts
nodes.summary: Extracts the newer 'Claim Approval' email's dollar figures (claimed, paid, excess, age contribution) by regex.

nodes.name: resolve_owed_by
nodes.summary: Determines whether the vet or Justin owes a requested document, read from the reply's To:/Cc: headers rather than defaulting to Justin.

nodes.name: extract_requested_document
nodes.summary: Extracts the verbatim document Petcover asked for from an info-request letter, stopping at its own boilerplate.

nodes.name: requested_document_date
nodes.summary: Parses the treatment date named inside a requested-document phrase, day-first (Australian format).

nodes.name: submission_group_id
nodes.summary: Derives a submission's short sayable id ('S6+7') from its claim ids.

nodes.name: correlate_ack
nodes.summary: Fallback correlation for a Petcover reply with no stored reference: finds the candidate submission by pet + condition text match, else the most-recently-sent one.

nodes.name: _already_recorded
nodes.summary: Whether this exact (email, claim, event type) has already been logged, so a re-read of processed mail doesn't duplicate events.

nodes.name: detach_reference
nodes.summary: Un-learns a wrongly-learned Petcover reference so the claim returns to the correlation pool for a re-read to route correctly.

nodes.name: transition_allowed
nodes.summary: Whether apply_event would move a claim at a given state on this event type, without writing anything — used by callers that must destroy state before the write.

nodes.name: apply_event
nodes.summary: The only writer of vet_claims.status: appends the event unconditionally, then writes the new state if the transition is legal, flags the claim if illegal, or no-ops if stateless.

nodes.name: _flag_claim
nodes.summary: Appends a reason to a claim's flag column rather than overwriting it.

nodes.name: _reverted_event_ids
nodes.summary: Ids of events a state_reverted event points at, for the fold to skip.

nodes.name: _fold
nodes.summary: Replays a claim's ordered event log into its current state, honoring the transition table and skipping illegal or reverted events.

nodes.name: project_state
nodes.summary: A claim's state as its own event log says it is, ignoring the stored column — the Phase-1 shadow projection.

nodes.name: project_all
nodes.summary: Bulk form of project_state for every claim in two queries.

nodes.name: state_projection_disagreements
nodes.summary: Claims whose stored status differs from what their event log projects — read-only diagnostic comparison.

nodes.name: process_reply
nodes.summary: Classifies one Petcover reply email and routes it to the claim(s) it concerns via (reference, serial), reference-only, or ack correlation, then applies the event and validates any stated settlement.

nodes.name: _validate_settlement
nodes.summary: Deterministic settlement check: expected = claimable minus per-condition excess (once per policy year), bounded by the annual cap, compared against what Petcover actually paid.

nodes.name: link_event
nodes.summary: Manually attaches an unlinked event to a claim without rewriting its status.

nodes.name: mark_sent
nodes.summary: Advances a claim (and every sibling sharing its draft) from drafted to sent, starting Petcover reply polling for the whole submission.

nodes.name: confirm_resolved
nodes.summary: Idempotently clears a needs-action flag (info request/suspension) on Justin's explicit confirmation.

nodes.name: _split_conditions
nodes.summary: Recovers a split claim's real per-condition subtotals from its stored item_conditions JSON.

nodes.name: _apply_excess_and_cap
nodes.summary: Fills each claim row's expected reimbursement in place, draining the per-condition excess in charge-date order then bounding by the annual cap.

nodes.name: visit_ledger
nodes.summary: Transaction-anchored dashboard rollup: one entry per vet bank charge with its claim(s) and excess/cap-aware expected-reimbursement estimate nested beneath.

nodes.name: history_rows
nodes.summary: Flattens visit_ledger into one row per claim for Telegram's /history, windowed by transaction date, oldest first.

nodes.name: _action_kind
nodes.summary: The single action a claim needs, factoring in split-proposal and unresolved-event sets not visible from the row alone.

nodes.name: _action_kind_from_row
nodes.summary: The part of the action determination that reads only the claim's own row — usable from a rendering path without extra DB queries.

nodes.name: pending_actions
nodes.summary: Everything waiting on Justin, one entry per claim, oldest charge first — the authoritative source both the agent and Telegram /actions read.

nodes.name: _collapse_submissions
nodes.summary: Folds submission-level actions (like mark_sent) down to one entry per submission instead of one per claim.

nodes.name: submissions_awaiting_reply
nodes.summary: What's been sent to Petcover and whether an answer came back, one entry per submission.

nodes.name: claim_detail
nodes.summary: Everything about one claim for 'why is #N like this' — transaction, invoice items, flag, and every status event with its recorded dollar figures.

nodes.name: treatment_date
nodes.summary: The earliest known treatment date on a claim's invoice, since Petcover's submission deadline is anchored on treatment, not the bank charge date.

nodes.name: unanswered_vet_requests
nodes.summary: Information requests the vet owes and nobody has answered, ordered by days remaining until the treatment-anchored submission deadline.

nodes.name: dismiss_mismatch
nodes.summary: Clears a settlement-mismatch flag once Justin has reviewed it, recording a mismatch_dismissed audit event.

nodes.name: mark_invoice_request_sent
nodes.summary: Records that Justin sent the invoice-request draft himself, opening the reply search window.

nodes.name: dashboard_lists
nodes.summary: Event-domain rollups for the dashboard: needs_action, settled reconciliation, and the manual-review queue of unlinked/unclassified events.

nodes.name: get_connection
nodes.summary: Context-managed SQLite connection in WAL mode with a busy timeout, so a host-side read and a container write on the same bind-mounted file don't lock each other out.

nodes.name: add_non_vet_pattern
nodes.summary: Records a non-vet merchant substring, returning False if it was blank or already present.

nodes.name: _invoice_date_plausible
nodes.summary: Whether an invoice's own date sits within the match window of the transaction date, guarding against a same-vet different-visit invoice slipping through.

nodes.name: _paid_on_charge_date
nodes.summary: Whether the document text itself states this invoice was paid on the bank charge's date, for invoices whose service date predates their payment date.

nodes.name: claimable_amount
nodes.summary: Sum of invoice line items excluding routine/preventive care keywords, falling back to the invoice total when unitemized.

nodes.name: _salvage_truncated
nodes.summary: Recovers a truncated LLM JSON reply by walking back to the last complete invoice object and closing the array.

nodes.name: _parse_invoices
nodes.summary: Parses the extraction LLM's reply into a list of invoice dicts, accepting the legacy single-invoice shape too.

nodes.name: _invoices_for_email
nodes.summary: One LLM extraction per email ever: returns the cached result or extracts and caches it; a failed extraction is not cached so it retries.

nodes.name: _vision_attempts_left
nodes.summary: Whether an email still has vision-OCR attempt budget remaining, consuming one attempt.

nodes.name: _page_jpeg
nodes.summary: Downscales a scanned invoice page's embedded image to JPEG for the vision model.

nodes.name: _vision_invoices
nodes.summary: Reads a scanned (image-only) invoice PDF page-by-page with the vision LLM as a fallback when the text pipeline finds nothing, refunding the attempt on a provider outage.

nodes.name: _build_queries
nodes.summary: Builds the Gmail search queries (narrow arrival window, wide open-ended window, spouse-address fallback) for finding a vet's invoice email.

nodes.name: _forward_confirms_vet
nodes.summary: Whether a forwarded invoice's quoted content actually names the vet, required before trusting a spouse-forwarded match.

nodes.name: _mark_matched
nodes.summary: Writes an invoice match onto a claim and applies the 'matched' state event.

nodes.name: _apply_match
nodes.summary: Writes the chosen invoice match, apportioning into a sibling claim when a second invoice explains the rest of the same bank charge.

nodes.name: _invoice_dates
nodes.summary: Every date an invoice bills for: its own header date plus any per-line-item dates.

nodes.name: find_visit_by_date
nodes.summary: Which visit a date names — checked against held claims first, then the email extraction cache — returning every match rather than guessing the nearest.

nodes.name: _already_claimed
nodes.summary: Whether another claim already carries this invoice, by invoice number or amount+date identity.

nodes.name: _pick_invoice
nodes.summary: The best-fitting invoice among candidates: under the ceiling, date-plausible, not already claimed, closest amount then closest date.

nodes.name: _oversized_candidate
nodes.summary: An invoice whose date matches the visit but whose total exceeds this charge — one invoice paid via several card charges.

nodes.name: _complement_for
nodes.summary: The other invoice this same charge also paid for, requiring the pair to sum to the charge within tolerance and each clear every match gate independently.

nodes.name: match_claim
nodes.summary: Searches Gmail for the invoice matching a claim's bank transaction across narrow/wide/spouse queries, pooling every invoice seen to also resolve one-charge-many-invoices, and advances the claim to matched on success.

nodes.name: _propose_split
nodes.summary: Records a merge proposal when this claim plus one sibling pending claim together explain an oversized invoice's total, so Justin only confirms which claim carries it.

nodes.name: merge_split_proposal
nodes.summary: Justin confirmed the merge: the claim with the larger bank charge carries the invoice, deterministically.

nodes.name: reject_split_proposal
nodes.summary: Justin said the charges are not the same invoice: closes the proposal and flags both claims for manual matching, never re-proposed.

nodes.name: resolve_split_proposal
nodes.summary: Attaches a multi-charge invoice to the chosen claim (matched) and closes the other claim as absorbed.

nodes.name: unmatch
nodes.summary: Rejects a wrong invoice match, remembering the rejected email and resetting the claim to pending_match for re-search — refused once the claim has been submitted.

nodes.name: _lookup_vet_email
nodes.summary: The vet's contact address: a manually-supplied override first, else the From header of a previously matched invoice email.

nodes.name: draft_invoice_request
nodes.summary: Drafts (never sends) an email asking the vet for a missing invoice.

nodes.name: init_db
nodes.summary: Executes the schema script, applies additive column migrations, and seeds the pets table — the FastAPI lifespan's first call.

nodes.name: _flag_claim
nodes.summary: Writes a flag string onto a claim.

nodes.name: main.py
nodes.summary: FastAPI application entry point: wires the dashboard/basic/health routes, starts the scheduler, Gmail polling, claims pipeline and Telegram bot on lifespan startup, and exposes the claim-mutation POST routes shared with Telegram.

nodes.name: message_log.py
nodes.summary: Durable log of every inbound/outbound Telegram message in one table, serving as training data, an audit trail, and an at-least-once replay queue for updates that arrived but never finished processing before a crash or restart.

nodes.name: netbank_csv.py
nodes.summary: Parses NetBank's headerless 4-column CSV export into bank transaction rows and imports them, skipping rows already stored by date+amount+merchant so overlapping re-uploads are safe.

nodes.name: lifespan
nodes.summary: FastAPI startup/shutdown hook: initializes the DB, starts the scheduler, Gmail polling, claims pipeline and Telegram polling.

nodes.name: dashboard
nodes.summary: Renders the main dashboard page: open tasks, due reminders, pets, and the transaction-anchored visit ledger.

nodes.name: basic_status
nodes.summary: Renders the phone-first stripped-down dashboard view as stacked cards.

nodes.name: _disagreement_count
nodes.summary: Count of state-projection disagreements for /health, reporting the failure as a value rather than silently as zero if the fold itself breaks.

nodes.name: health
nodes.summary: Health-check endpoint reporting app version, Telegram polling status, state-projection disagreements and message-log stats.

nodes.name: upload_transactions
nodes.summary: Dashboard POST route parsing an uploaded NetBank CSV and running the claims pipeline once.

nodes.name: _describe
nodes.summary: Classifies an inbound Telegram update into (kind, summary) text for the log — handles taps, edits, commands, text and non-text messages.

nodes.name: record_inbound
nodes.summary: Writes the arrival row for an inbound update before handlers run, deduping Telegram redeliveries by update_id.

nodes.name: mark_processed
nodes.summary: Settles a processed row, refusing to clear one that already carries an error so it stays in the replay queue.

nodes.name: pending
nodes.summary: Inbound updates still owed (not yet processed), within the replay window.

nodes.name: replay_pending
nodes.summary: Re-runs updates that arrived but never finished processing, after polling starts so Telegram's own redeliveries dedupe by update_id.

nodes.name: expire_queue
nodes.summary: Stops replaying updates older than the replay window while keeping the rows as training data.

nodes.name: iter_jsonl
nodes.summary: Streams the whole message log as JSONL, oldest first, for reinforcement learning.

nodes.name: _parse_row
nodes.summary: Parses one NetBank CSV row into a date/amount/merchant dict, raising CsvParseError on any malformed field rather than inserting partial data.

nodes.name: import_rows
nodes.summary: Inserts parsed transaction rows, skipping ones already stored by date+amount+merchant.

nodes.name: parse
nodes.summary: Parses NetBank's headerless CSV export into transaction dicts, stopping at the first malformed row rather than inserting partial data.

nodes.name: stats
nodes.summary: Queue depth and last-inbound timestamp for the /health endpoint.

nodes.name: mark_failed
nodes.summary: Records why an update failed and leaves processed_at NULL so it stays in the replay queue.

nodes.name: pipeline.py
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the scheduled claims tick: watches Telegram polling health, matches pending claims to invoices, drafts claim forms, polls Petcover for status replies, and pushes Telegram notifications/nudges — the top-level loop tying every claims module together (logical orchestration layer, never a separate deployable per ADR-0006).

nodes.name: status_labels.py
nodes.summary: The single place a claim's status is turned into human-readable wording and 'what's needed' phrasing, shared by the dashboard templates, Telegram cards and pipeline notify text so no surface can drift out of sync.

nodes.name: telegram_bot.py
nodes.summary: The Telegram bot surface: slash commands, inline-keyboard callback handling, the conversational-agent chat path, and durable logging wrappers (LoggedApplication, LoggedBot) that record every update/message for replay and audit.

nodes.name: _alert_rate_limited
nodes.summary: Sends a Telegram ops alert at most a capped number of times per rolling 24h, tracked in the ops_alerts table so a restart can't reset the count.

nodes.name: _ensure_gmail_auth
nodes.summary: Probes Gmail credentials once per tick, alerting (rate-limited) on auth death and confirming recovery exactly once when it clears.

nodes.name: _latest_settlement_detail
nodes.summary: The dollar breakdown for a claim's settlement, checking both the 'approved' and 'settled' event types for whichever carries figures.

nodes.name: _submission_label
nodes.summary: A submission's Telegram-friendly identifier: the Petcover reference once known, else the derived group id, always with claim ids.

nodes.name: _summarize_drafted
nodes.summary: Builds the Telegram notification text for a drafted batch ready to send.

nodes.name: _invoice_lines
nodes.summary: Itemised invoice line items as display strings.

nodes.name: _summarize_matched_flag
nodes.summary: Builds the Telegram notification text explaining why a matched claim is still blocked (bad invoice match, missing pet, etc.).

nodes.name: _summarize_group
nodes.summary: Dispatches to the right per-status notification text builder for a claim group.

nodes.name: notify_split_proposals
nodes.summary: Pushes the one-invoice/several-charges merge picker to Telegram, once per proposal, attaching the invoice pages themselves when available.

nodes.name: _latest_settled_email_id
nodes.summary: The email carrying a claim's settlement figures, for either letter template.

nodes.name: _review_pdf
nodes.summary: The vet/Petcover document behind a needs-review flag, recovered via the matched email, the settlement email, or a best-effort Gmail subject search.

nodes.name: notify_claim_states
nodes.summary: Pushes a Telegram message when a claim group enters a state worth hearing about, attaching the right inline keyboard and review PDF, deduped on (status, flag).

nodes.name: reconcile_sent_invoice_requests
nodes.summary: Checks Gmail's own SENT/DRAFT labels to detect invoice-request drafts Justin has since sent, since the dashboard's manual confirm click is often missed.

nodes.name: nudge_stale_actions
nodes.summary: Once-daily reminder covering every action that has gone stale, since the change-feed notifier only announces a status change once.

nodes.name: _visit_line
nodes.summary: Which visit a requested date names, for the vet-chase nudge message, stating explicitly what evidence supports the match.

nodes.name: nudge_unanswered_vet_requests
nodes.summary: Weekly reminder of every information request the vet owes and nobody answered, with clinic contact, document name and deadline.

nodes.name: _maybe_draft_invoice_request
nodes.summary: Drafts (never sends) a vet invoice-request email once a pending claim's match window has elapsed with nothing found.

nodes.name: _claims_touched_since
nodes.summary: Claim ids that gained an event after a given event id.

nodes.name: poll_petcover_status
nodes.summary: Polls Petcover's status-reply senders for new mail and records each via claim_status.process_reply, oldest-first so a settlement never processes before its own acknowledgement.

nodes.name: _matched_claims
nodes.summary: Claims currently at status matched.

nodes.name: _draft_matched_claims
nodes.summary: Extracts invoice files for matched claims then drafts fully-ready ones in per-pet batches of up to 4, running per-field flagging for anything not ready.

nodes.name: _watchdog_telegram_polling
nodes.summary: Detects a dead Telegram polling task and restarts the whole process via SIGTERM, since compose is configured to restart unless-stopped.

nodes.name: compare_state_projection
nodes.summary: Shadow-mode diagnostic comparing every claim's event-log projection to its stored status column, logging (not fixing) any disagreement.

nodes.name: run_once
nodes.summary: The scheduled claims tick: watchdog, classification, matching, drafting, Petcover polling and notification, isolating one claim's failure from the rest.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Registers the claims pipeline, stale-action nudge, vet-request nudge and message-queue expiry as APScheduler jobs.

nodes.name: short_document
nodes.summary: A chip-sized name for a recognized requested-document kind, or None if unrecognized — falls back to who-owes-it wording rather than inventing a name.

nodes.name: label
nodes.summary: Display wording for one claim's status, factoring in whether a 'matched' claim needs a condition/pet or is blocked, and who owes an info request.

nodes.name: needs
nodes.summary: The one-line 'what's needed' phrase for the phone-first dashboard view.

nodes.name: _ack_user_message
nodes.summary: Group -1 handler acking every authorized user message before real handlers run, so slow LLM turns don't feel dead.

nodes.name: handle_vetemail
nodes.summary: Pure logic for /vetemail: stores a vet's contact email for invoice requests.

nodes.name: handle_notvet
nodes.summary: Pure logic for /notvet: adds a merchant substring to the non-vet list.

nodes.name: mark_command
nodes.summary: Async /mark command adapter parsing claim id and condition/reviewed argument.

nodes.name: pet_command
nodes.summary: Async /pet command adapter parsing claim id and pet name.

nodes.name: process_command
nodes.summary: Async /process command adapter parsing claim id.

nodes.name: _single_claim_id_command
nodes.summary: Adapter factory for commands whose only argument is a claim id (/sent, /resolved), shared to avoid duplicating the parsing boilerplate.

nodes.name: vetemail_command
nodes.summary: Async /vetemail command adapter, splitting merchant name from the trailing email token.

nodes.name: _history_page
nodes.summary: Renders one /history page's PNG + caption + clamped page numbers, re-reading the DB each time so a changed claim renders current.

nodes.name: history_command
nodes.summary: Async /history command sending the first claim-history page as a photo.

nodes.name: _action_card_text
nodes.summary: Builds one action's HTML card text, itemising every member for a submission-level action.

nodes.name: _action_keyboard
nodes.summary: Reuses the existing per-action inline keyboard for an action card's kind.

nodes.name: actions_command
nodes.summary: Async /actions command sending the actions-summary photo plus one card per actionable item, capped and reporting how many were held back.

nodes.name: prior_conditions
nodes.summary: Conditions previously claimed for a pet, offered as one-tap options.

nodes.name: condition_keyboard
nodes.summary: Inline keyboard of prior conditions plus 'Other' and (when multi-item) 'Split by item' buttons.

nodes.name: _invoice_items
nodes.summary: A claim's invoice line items for the per-item condition split flow.

nodes.name: _record_and_advance
nodes.summary: Records the current split item's condition and advances to the next, or applies the finished split.

nodes.name: merge_bill_keyboard
nodes.summary: Confirm/reject inline keyboard for a one-invoice-several-charges merge proposal.

nodes.name: _execute_action
nodes.summary: Runs a confirmed mutation through the same domain functions the slash commands use — the actual write, only after a Confirm tap.

nodes.name: on_callback
nodes.summary: Dispatches every inline-keyboard tap by its callback_data prefix to the matching domain action.

nodes.name: db_backup.py

nodes.summary: One-off CLI entry point that triggers a single immediate Drive DB backup by calling db_backup.backup_once(), useful for testing after re-running Gmail auth or for an ad-hoc backup.

nodes.name: gmail_auth.py

nodes.name: reextract_item_dates.py

nodes.name: _snapshot_db_bytes
nodes.summary: Safely copies the live SQLite database to a temp file using sqlite3's own backup API (avoiding a raw file copy against a WAL-mode DB) and returns the bytes.

nodes.name: backup_once

nodes.name: gemini.py
nodes.summary: Google Gemini API wrapper providing rate-limited text extraction and vision-capable image analysis; the sole vision backend per ADR-0010, with every call outcome logged to the database for observability.

nodes.name: llm.py
nodes.summary: Provider-agnostic LLM access layer (ADR-0009/ADR-0017) unifying Groq and OpenAI behind chat()/extract()/extract_vision(), with per-model retry, daily-token-budget fallback across Groq models, and delegation to Gemini for vision -- the only module allowed to import a provider SDK.

nodes.name: scheduler.py

nodes.name: ssl_compat.py
nodes.summary: Monkey-patches Python's SSLContext to trust the OS certificate store instead of certifi, working around a corporate TLS-intercepting proxy for outbound HTTPS calls such as the Gemini SDK.
nodes.languageNotes: Patches SSLContext.wrap_socket/wrap_bio at the urllib3 layer -- a deliberate global monkeypatch chosen to route around TLS interception without touching per-request code.

nodes.name: tasks.py
nodes.summary: Task and reminder capture: creates tasks (optionally extracting a follow-up date via the LLM), records outcomes, and is the entry point for Gmail-derived task candidates.

nodes.name: vet_detection.py

nodes.name: GeminiUnavailableError
nodes.summary: Exception raised when the Gemini API fails after all retries; callers must surface it rather than swallow it.

nodes.name: _RateLimiter
nodes.summary: In-memory sliding-window rate limiter (calls-per-minute), shared by both the Gemini client and the generic LLM client; single-process only by design.
nodes.languageNotes: Deque-based sliding window, correct only for a single process -- matches the project's single-user/local deployment.

nodes.name: _log_call
nodes.summary: Writes a row to the LLM call-log table recording purpose, success, latency and error for every Gemini invocation; reused by llm.py as the shared call-logging path.

nodes.name: extract
nodes.summary: Public entry point for plain-text extraction via Gemini; delegates to _generate.

nodes.name: extract_image
nodes.summary: Public entry point for vision extraction: wraps a JPEG as a Gemini content Part and delegates to _generate; the project's sole vision-capable path (ADR-0010).

nodes.name: _generate
nodes.summary: Core retry loop against the Gemini SDK: rate-limits, retries up to MAX_RETRIES with exponential backoff, distinguishes rate-limit errors from other failures, logs every attempt, and raises GeminiUnavailableError (never swallowed) if all retries fail.

nodes.name: LLMUnavailableError
nodes.summary: Exception raised when the configured LLM provider fails after retries or is misconfigured; never swallowed by callers.

nodes.name: _openai_client
nodes.summary: Lazily constructs and caches a singleton OpenAI-compatible client for the configured provider (Groq or OpenAI), raising LLMUnavailableError if the API key is missing.

nodes.name: _try_model
nodes.summary: Retry loop for a single model: acquires the shared rate limiter, calls the chat completions API, logs each attempt, and classifies failures (daily-budget exhaustion, malformed tool call, bad request) to decide whether retrying helps.

nodes.name: _completion
nodes.summary: Drives model fallback: tries the primary model, and on Groq daily-budget exhaustion falls through to each configured fallback model in turn (ADR-0017), surfacing which model finally answered or raising LLMUnavailableError if all are exhausted.

nodes.name: _assistant_turn
nodes.summary: Builds the assistant message dict for a chat turn, including any tool calls, from the raw provider response.

nodes.name: chat
nodes.summary: Multi-turn tool-calling chat loop: sends messages plus a tool schema to the LLM, executes any requested tool implementations, appends results, and repeats until the model stops calling tools or max_iterations is reached.

nodes.name: extract_vision
nodes.summary: Delegates vision extraction to Gemini (the only vision-capable backend, ADR-0010) regardless of the configured text provider.

nodes.name: extract
nodes.summary: Plain-text extraction: uses Gemini directly if configured as the provider, otherwise runs a single-turn chat() call.

nodes.name: schedule_reminder
nodes.summary: Inserts a pending reminder row for a task and schedules an APScheduler job to fire at the given time.

nodes.name: patch_requests_to_use_os_trust_store
nodes.summary: Monkey-patches SSLContext.wrap_socket/wrap_bio so outbound HTTPS connections validate against the OS trust store rather than certifi's bundle, working around a corporate TLS-intercepting proxy.

nodes.name: _extract_follow_up

nodes.name: Dockerfile

nodes.languageNotes: APP_VERSION is declared as an ARG/ENV after the pip install layer specifically so version bumps don't invalidate the dependency cache.

nodes.name: apply.md
nodes.summary: Claude Code slash-command definition for /opsx:apply — implements pending tasks from an OpenSpec change, reading context artifacts (proposal/specs/design/tasks) and looping through the task list until all tasks are done or a blocker forces a pause.
nodes.languageNotes: Claude Code slash-command markdown with YAML frontmatter (name/description/category/tags) that drives command registration; body is agent instructions, not prose documentation.

nodes.name: archive.md
nodes.summary: Slash-command definition for /opsx:archive — verifies artifact and task completion, optionally triggers a delta-spec sync via the openspec-sync-specs skill, then moves a finished OpenSpec change into a dated archive directory.

nodes.name: explore.md
nodes.summary: Slash-command definition for /opsx:explore — a non-implementing 'thinking partner' stance for investigating ideas, the codebase, and tradeoffs before a decision crystallizes into an OpenSpec change proposal.

nodes.name: propose.md
nodes.summary: Slash-command definition for /opsx:propose — scaffolds a new OpenSpec change directory and generates its proposal.md, design.md, and tasks.md artifacts in dependency order, ready for /opsx:apply.

nodes.name: sync.md
nodes.summary: Slash-command definition for /opsx:sync — an agent-driven merge of a change's delta specs (ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED/RENAMED requirements) into the project's main OpenSpec specs, using intelligent partial-update merging rather than wholesale replacement.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: Root project instructions for AI-assisted sessions: hard non-negotiable rules (never send email, never guess required claim fields, never store bank logins, failures must be visible), hard-won domain rules for the claims pipeline, and operational gotchas around LLM backends, Gmail OAuth, and the .env/data-dir split between the main checkout and the deploy worktree.

nodes.name: CONTEXT.md
nodes.summary: Domain vocabulary glossary that pins down claims-side terms (Claim, Submission, Condition Thread, Serial, Excess, Policy Year, Invoice, Charge) and assistant-side terms (Task, Follow-up, Reminder, Sweep), each with an explicit list of words to avoid, to keep chat/dashboard/insurer-facing language unambiguous.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Project overview describing the end-to-end vet-claim automation pipeline (bank-charge detection, Gmail invoice matching, Petcover claim-form filling, reply/status tracking), the invoice-matching algorithm's ceiling/date/dedup rules and special-case handling, the complete list of third-party API calls, storage layout, and setup/run instructions.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml
nodes.summary: Single-service Docker Compose config that builds the FastAPI app from ./app, stamps APP_VERSION from the git SHA via a build arg (else it warns as 'unknown'), loads secrets from app/.env, and bind-mounts the shared host data directory (SQLite DB + Gmail credentials) into the container at /data so the container and main checkout use one data store.
nodes.languageNotes: The bind mount is a deliberate single-source-of-truth choice (marked with a 'ponytail: one data dir, not two' comment) rather than an oversight — the feature worktree ships new code only, never its own copy of the data.

nodes.name: 2026-07-20-vet-claim-pipeline-fixes.md
nodes.summary: Investigation log for a session where the vet-claim pipeline was found silently stuck: documents four bugs found and fixed (Gmail task-capture noise filtering, invoice-request-sent reconciliation, an unverified spouse-forward fallback causing false matches, and a missing invoice-date plausibility check) plus one known-but-unfixed limitation (scanned PDF invoices have no OCR support).
nodes.languageNotes: Written as a dated findings-and-fixes log with one section per issue, each stating symptom, root cause, fix, and live verification evidence — not a design doc.

nodes.name: CROSS-BRANCH-NOTES.md
nodes.summary: Handoff note from the telegram/LLM branch to the dashboard branch: a new claim-drafting guard keeps a claim at status `matched` (not `drafted`) until an itemised invoice is attached, and new `pets.annual_excess`/`annual_cap` columns need an explicit DB migration since `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` won't alter the already-created live table.

nodes.name: failure-modes.md
nodes.summary: A living index — not a diary — of past project failures (tests green while code was wrong, real-data assumptions that turned out false, process/decision-trail slips, operational outages), each paired with the specific check that now catches it or an explicit 'no check yet', so the team doesn't burn tokens rediscovering an issue already recorded elsewhere.
nodes.languageNotes: Structured as reference tables (what happened / recorded in / check that catches it now) rather than prose; deliberately terse pointers into ADRs, BACKLOG.md, CLAUDE.md and commit hashes rather than restating them.

nodes.name: 0001-gemini-only-llm-backend-for-v1.md
nodes.summary: Records the v1 decision to send every LLM request to Gemini 2.5 Flash's free tier as the sole backend, rejecting a local-Ollama+Claude hybrid and a Claude-only option to avoid upfront cost and tuning work. Marked superseded by ADR-0009 once the free tier proved insufficient.

nodes.name: 0002-python-fastapi-apscheduler-sqlite-stack.md
nodes.summary: Establishes the core stack for the single-user local app: Python/FastAPI for the dashboard, APScheduler with a SQLite jobstore for restart-safe scheduling, and SQLite for storage, all in one Docker Compose service.

nodes.name: 0003-dashboard-only-reminders-no-push.md
nodes.summary: Decides v1 reminders surface only on the local FastAPI dashboard, deferring any push-notification channel (Telegram/Pushover) as out of scope to keep the capture-schedule-follow-up loop narrow.

nodes.name: 0004-gmail-polling-over-push-watch.md
nodes.summary: Chooses periodic Gmail API polling (default 5 min, deduped by message ID) over push/watch notifications, since push requires a public HTTPS endpoint incompatible with the local-only, no-exposed-port deployment.

nodes.name: 0005-windows-strict-x509-ssl-workaround.md
nodes.summary: Documents a targeted patch to ssl.SSLContext.wrap_socket that clears VERIFY_X509_STRICT to fix CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED errors caused by a locally-installed EDR root CA on Windows, after ruling out requests/urllib3 context injection and pip-system-certs as non-functional.
nodes.languageNotes: Notable as a machine-specific operational workaround baked into application code (app/openclaw/ssl_compat.py) rather than a portable library fix.

nodes.name: 0006-claims-service-logical-boundary-single-process.md
nodes.summary: Decides the vet-claims service (vet_detection, invoice_matching, claim_forms, claim_status, orchestrated by pipeline) remains a logical module boundary inside the one FastAPI app rather than a separate deployable, since SQLite is single-writer and there is only one user.

nodes.name: 0007-bank-charge-ceiling-invoice-matching.md
nodes.summary: Redefines the bank charge as a ceiling rather than an equality target for invoice matching, and makes the claim form carry the claimable subtotal (line items minus non-claimable keywords) instead of the raw bank amount, fixing real card-surcharge and multi-invoice cases.

nodes.name: 0008-append-only-claim-status-event-log.md
nodes.summary: Introduces an append-only claim_status_events log where a claim's current status is its latest event, and 'needs your action' states persist until Justin's explicit confirm-resolved click, so Petcover's inconsistent reply ordering can never silently clear an open request.

nodes.name: 0009-provider-agnostic-llm-backend.md
nodes.summary: Supersedes ADR-0001 with a provider-agnostic llm.py seam (chat/extract) selected by env var, defaulting to Groq's free-tier llama-3.3-70b-versatile after Cerebras' free tier proved sold-out; an amendment later corrects the 'no context cap' claim and notes the quota mitigation was superseded by ADR-0017.

nodes.name: 0010-vision-ocr-fallback-scanned-invoices.md
nodes.summary: Adds a Gemini vision-OCR fallback (llm.extract_vision) for photo-scanned invoice PDFs with no text layer, gated to a narrow trigger and hard-capped at 3 attempts per email with an outage refund, plus new invoice-matching guards against false-matching bulk-scan invoices.

nodes.name: 0011-condition-thread-correlation.md
nodes.summary: Replaces per-submission Petcover reference correlation with a Condition Thread entity (pet, reference) that persists across years, routing events by reference+serial and mapping acknowledgements to claims via condition text then send-recency; an amendment adds a second serial format ('Treatment number: N').

nodes.name: 0012-continuation-defaults-true.md
nodes.summary: Sets the Petcover claim form's continuation checkbox to default true on every generated form as an interim measure until Condition-Thread-derived continuation is implemented, since most claims are ongoing conditions and Justin reviews every draft anyway.

nodes.name: 0013-excess-accrual-gates-submission.md
nodes.summary: Holds a matched claim until its condition's accrued claimable exceeds the $150 annual excess before drafting, adding a below_excess status distinct from declined; an amendment corrects the policy-year bucketing to use each claim's own transaction date rather than 'now', with a closed-policy-year default.

nodes.name: 0014-durable-telegram-message-log.md
nodes.summary: Introduces a single telegram_messages table recording every inbound/outbound Telegram message as an RL dataset, audit trail, and at-least-once replay queue, with asymmetric retention (queue expires, log never deletes); an amendment moves replay to a background task so it can't block HTTP startup.

nodes.name: 0015-restart-on-dead-updater-and-alerting-levels.md
nodes.summary: Makes a dead Telegram updater trigger a rate-limited alert followed by process restart via Compose, defines what ERROR/WARNING/INFO log levels mean, and bakes deploy identity from git SHA; an amendment records that alerting itself depends on the DB and silently failed during a DB outage.

nodes.name: 0016-telegram-agent-tool-surface.md
nodes.summary: Widens the Telegram agent's tool surface (narrowing, not deleting, the no-mailbox-access rule) to add on-demand idempotent sweeps and claim-detail lookups, and rejects MCP since the tools are same-process Python functions with no vendor/process boundary to justify it; an amendment corrects a wrongly 'no daily token limit' claim.

nodes.name: 0017-per-model-daily-budget-fallback.md
nodes.summary: Adds automatic per-model fallback within Groq (four models with independent daily token budgets) when the primary model's daily quota is exhausted, disclosing which model answered, superseding ADR-0009's manual-provider-swap mitigation for this specific failure mode.

nodes.name: 0018-host-side-db-access-is-read-only.md
nodes.summary: Mandates read-only (mode=ro) host-side SQLite connections after a plain read-write connect() checkpointed and deleted the WAL sidecar files, causing a total container-side DB outage due to a Docker Desktop bind-mount caching bug.

nodes.name: 0019-one-invoice-several-pets.md
nodes.summary: Defines a one-claim-row-per-pet data model for a single invoice covering several pets, splitting shares in invoice_data with Justin-supplied amounts pre-submission only; a same-day amendment corrects the diagnosed case to two separate invoices under one surcharge-adjusted charge and adds automatic charge apportionment across invoices.

nodes.name: 0020-re-reading-petcover-mail-may-not-write-status.md
nodes.summary: Allows re-reading already-processed Petcover mail to append events and learn references without ever writing claim status/flag directly, and derives who owes an information request from the letter's To/Cc recipients rather than its sender; four dated amendments track document/date extraction, a weekly vet-nudge cadence, a treatment-date correction, and a correction to an incomplete prior correction.

nodes.name: 0021-status-is-state-label-is-who-holds-it.md
nodes.summary: ADR deciding that a claim's stored `vet_claims.status` stays pipeline state while the dashboard label becomes a separate, single mapping in `status_labels.py` — a `matched` claim's label is derived from the action-determination logic, and an info-request label names who owes the document rather than reusing the word 'suspended'.

nodes.name: 0022-claim-status-is-a-declared-state-machine.md
nodes.summary: ADR establishing claim status as a declared state machine: event types are classified as state-changing, stateless, or backfill; `claim_status.apply_event` becomes the sole writer of `vet_claims.status`, checking a `TRANSITIONS` table before writing; and `status` is reframed as a projection folded from `claim_status_events` with the column as its cache.
nodes.languageNotes: Phase 1 (enforcement + shadow projection) is shipped; Phase 2 (projection becomes authoritative, revert_state, claim timeline) is designed but not built.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: OpenClaw is a personal assistant that turns a vet bank charge into a ready-to-send Petcover insurance claim, plus a lightweight task/reminder capture system from Gmail. The README lays out the three hard promises the whole codebase is built around: never send email (Gmail drafts only), never store bank logins (manual CSV upload), and never guess required claim fields (flag instead of infer). Keep these three rules in mind — they explain design choices you'll see repeated in almost every module ahead.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: main.py is the FastAPI entry point: on startup it wires the dashboard/health routes, starts the APScheduler, kicks off Gmail polling, boots the claims pipeline, and launches the Telegram bot — all as part of one process's lifespan hook. It also exposes the claim-mutation POST routes that both the dashboard and Telegram share, so there is exactly one code path for changing a claim's state no matter which surface triggered it.

tour.title: The Data Layer
tour.description: db.py defines every SQLite table (claims, status events, split proposals, Telegram messages) and hands out WAL-mode connections with a busy timeout — everything else in the app reads and writes through this one module. config.py sits alongside it, centralizing every environment-variable-driven setting (LLM keys, Gmail paths, owner/bank details, Telegram config) loaded once at import time via dotenv. Together these two files are the foundation the rest of the pipeline depends on, which is why they rank among the highest fan-in files in the whole graph.

tour.title: Detecting a Vet Charge
tour.description: vet_detection.py is where the claims pipeline begins: it classifies an imported bank transaction as vet-related or not, using keyword rules and learned non-vet patterns first and only falling back to an LLM call for ambiguous merchant/category combinations. A match creates a pending row in the vet_claims table from Step 3 — the first domino in the chain that ends with a claim draft. netbank_csv.py feeds this step, parsing NetBank's headerless CSV export into transaction rows and safely skipping duplicates on re-upload, since bank login credentials are never stored — only manual CSV uploads are trusted.

tour.title: Matching the Invoice
tour.description: Once a charge is flagged as vet-related, invoice_matching.py searches Gmail for the invoice that explains it, extracting invoice data via an LLM call (falling back to vision OCR for scanned PDF attachments) and resolving tricky apportionment cases — one charge covering many invoices, or one invoice split across many charges. This is the module ADR-0007's ceiling rule lives in: the bank charge is a ceiling on the claim, never an equality target, because card surcharges and multi-invoice charges make exact matches unreliable.
tour.languageLesson: Python's LLM-extraction-with-fallback pattern here — regex/keyword rules first, vision OCR only as a last resort — keeps token spend low while still handling the messy real-world documents that pure rules can't parse.

tour.title: Filling the Claim Form and Tracking Its Status
tour.description: claim_forms.py fills the Petcover PDF form and stages a Gmail draft (never sent) once a charge and invoice are matched — this is the only place a claim actually gets drafted. claim_status.py is the single writer of a claim's status: it classifies Petcover's reply emails, applies transitions against an append-only event log, and computes the excess/cap reimbursement ledger, so nothing ever mutates status except through this one state machine. Both modules rank near the top of the fan-in list, meaning almost everything downstream — the dashboard, Telegram, the pipeline itself — reads through them rather than tracking claim state independently.

tour.title: Orchestrating the Pipeline
tour.description: pipeline.py is the scheduled tick that ties every claims module together: it watches Telegram polling health, matches pending claims to invoices, drafts claim forms, polls Petcover for status replies, and pushes notifications — calling out to vet_detection, invoice_matching, claim_forms, and claim_status in sequence. Per ADR-0006, this is a logical orchestration layer, never a separate deployable, which is why it has the highest fan-out of any claims module. status_labels.py works alongside it as the single place a claim's status becomes human-readable wording, shared by the dashboard, Telegram cards, and pipeline notifications so no surface can drift out of sync with another.

tour.title: The LLM Gateway
tour.description: llm.py is the provider-agnostic gateway (ADR-0009/ADR-0017) that every extraction and chat call in the pipeline goes through — unifying Groq and OpenAI behind chat()/extract()/extract_vision(), with per-model retry and automatic daily-token-budget fallback across Groq's models. It's the only module allowed to import a provider SDK directly. gemini.py is the sole vision-capable backend it delegates to (ADR-0010), and ssl_compat.py is the quiet dependency underneath both: it monkey-patches Python's SSLContext so outbound HTTPS calls survive a corporate TLS-intercepting proxy.
tour.languageLesson: llm.py's daily-token-budget fallback is a practical example of Python's try/except-driven retry chains: when one model's budget is exhausted, the same call transparently retries against the next model and reports which one actually answered.

tour.title: Gmail Integration
tour.description: gmail_client.py is the thin wrapper around the Gmail API that both invoice_matching (Step 5) and gmail_ingest depend on: it loads/refreshes OAuth credentials and extracts full message text, including decoded PDF attachment content, since settlement dollar breakdowns live only in the PDF, never the email body. This module has no business logic of its own — it exists purely so every other module talks to Gmail through one place, making credential handling and API quirks a solved problem elsewhere in the codebase.

tour.title: The Telegram Interface
tour.description: telegram_bot.py is the highest fan-out interface module: slash commands, inline-keyboard callbacks, the conversational chat path, and durable logging wrappers that record every update for replay after a crash. agent.py builds the conversational layer on top of it — exposing read-only query tools plus propose_* action tools to llm.chat's tool loop, where act tools never mutate directly, only queue a proposal the bot renders as a Confirm button. claim_card.py renders claim history and action summaries as PNG images via Pillow, since Telegram's plain text can't produce aligned tables or status chips, and message_log.py is the durable log underneath all of it, giving at-least-once replay for updates that arrived but never finished processing.

tour.title: The Assistant Side: Tasks and Reminders
tour.description: Alongside the claims pipeline, OpenClaw also captures tasks and reminders. gmail_ingest.py polls the inbox on a schedule and filters out marketing/automated senders with keyword heuristics (not an LLM call, to conserve the tight daily token budget) before handing genuine replies to tasks.py, which creates task rows and optionally extracts a follow-up date. reminders.py and scheduler.py close the loop, bridging the task store with the single process-wide APScheduler instance introduced back in Step 2's startup sequence.

tour.title: Containerization and Deployment
tour.description: The Dockerfile builds the FastAPI app on a python:3.13-slim base, installing the DejaVu fonts claim_card.py (Step 10) needs for Pillow rendering, and stamping an APP_VERSION build arg so every Telegram message logged in Step 10 can be traced back to a commit. docker-compose.yml wraps it as a single-service deployment: it loads secrets from app/.env and bind-mounts the shared host data directory into the container at /data, so the container and the main checkout read and write the exact same SQLite database from db.py in Step 3.
tour.languageLesson: Docker build-arg stamping (APP_VERSION) is a lightweight alternative to a full CI versioning pipeline: the git SHA is baked in at image-build time and surfaces at runtime for tracing, without needing a separate release-tagging system.

tour.title: Verifying It All Works
tour.description: test_core.py is an assert-based smoke suite (no pytest) covering the entire backend seen so far — vet detection, invoice matching, the claim-status lifecycle, claim forms, LLM retry/fallback, and CSV import — run with a plain Python invocation and fully hermetic: every LLM key is force-blanked and vision extraction is stubbed, so running the tests never spends a token. test_telegram.py does the same for the interface layer from Step 10, exercising bot commands, notification dedup, action cards, and split/merge flows. Together they're the safety net that lets every module explored in this tour keep changing without silently breaking another.
